limit_order_matching_in_progress.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_matching_in_progress.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade guard is evaluated during limit order matching

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (e.g., base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21)
matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before the zero-cost trade guard is evaluated during limit order matching

zero_cost_guard_triggered.meaning: the zero-cost trade guard triggers (fires) during limit order matching
zero_cost_guard_triggered.checkpoint: at zero-cost trade guard evaluation during limit order matching

one_side_receives_without_sending.meaning: one side receives tokens without sending any
one_side_receives_without_sending.checkpoint: at zero-cost trade guard evaluation during limit order matching

limit_order_matching_reverts.meaning: limit order matching (partial or full) reverts
limit_order_matching_reverts.checkpoint: after zero-cost trade guard evaluation during limit order matching

assumptions: The zero-cost trade guard is the check whose triggering is governed by the stated intent.
The report's 'one side receives tokens without sending any' is treated as a qualitative observable condition.

unresolved.description: The intent states the guard should trigger ONLY when one side receives without sending, i.e. a necessary condition (guard_triggered implies one_side_receives_without_sending); the required_effect template expresses a sufficient-condition conjunction (guard_triggered AND one_side_receives_without_sending), which does not faithfully encode the 'only when' direction.
The exact zero-cost check expression and its operands are not fully quoted in prose, so the guard-triggered observable cannot be bound to a concrete numeric expression.

limitations: The impact text describes scope (all limit order matching, partial and full) rather than a distinct observable outcome; the V witness uses a grounded revert occurrence Boolean.
Fill orders being unaffected is not encoded because it is outside the selected impact's direct observable.
The disjoint-bits precondition is encoded as a qualitative Boolean because the report gives only illustrative examples, not a single defining expression.
